title: Admin Login Bypass via SQL Injection
impact: Attacker authenticates as the administrator without knowing the password, gaining full access to the admin account and any privileged functionality.
remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements instead of building SQL with string concatenation, and validate and sanitize all user input server-side.

title: Data Extraction via UNION-based SQL Injection
payload_used: apple')) UNION SELECT id%2C email%2C password%2C '4'%2C '5'%2C '6'%2C '7'%2C '8'%2C '9' FROM Users--
impact: Attacker dumps data from unrelated database tables (e.g. user emails and password hashes) through a search endpoint that was never meant to expose that data.
remediation: Use parameterized queries, apply least-privilege database accounts, and never build SQL by concatenating raw user input.

title: Reflected XSS via Search Field
impact: Attacker crafts a malicious link that, when clicked by a victim, executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session (e.g. for phishing or session theft).
remediation: Encode/escape user input before reflecting it into HTML, and deploy a Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict inline script execution.

title: Stored XSS via Feedback/Comment Field
impact: The payload is saved server-side and executes automatically for every user (including admins) who later views the page, enabling persistent session hijacking or defacement.
remediation: Sanitize and encode input before storing it and again before rendering it (e.g. with a library like DOMPurify), and apply a strict CSP.
